findings.issue: Reuse validates live ROOT against recorded input metadata and the previous root snapshot,but never rehashes the actual private fixture's source/config files against expected inputs or compares its current BUILD_ID/emitted serving artifacts with the retained verified handoff. It reads the current BUILD_ID and current emitted files afterward and can publish them as a new reusable verified handoff. Served HTML/static equality is checked only against that current fixture,not the expected verified build;HTML is not asserted to contain the expected build ID. A changed/rebuilt/damaged fixture can therefore be certified against unrelated recorded source metadata while the root remains unchanged.
findings.impact: This defeats the source-to-built-artifact reuse guard central to repeatable autonomous QA. An ordinary stale or replaced private build is not necessarily detected before its new identities overwrite prior handoff records. The currently inspected pre-header fixture is valid;this finding concerns the submitted guard's behavior,not observed tampering or a demand for immutable forensic attestation.
findings.reproduction: Read-only Node24 in-memory control executed the actual extracted reuse-entry block with matching recorded root inputs and baseline,but a stub filesystem offering a different private BUILD_ID/fixture bytes. The block accepted;its only read was before-verify.json.gz and it made zero private fixture/build reads. Later source flow adopts current BUILD_ID/files without comparison to the expected handoff. Full verify/reuse was NOT executed and no real artifact was changed.
findings.fix_direction: Before reuse checks/start,validate actual private source/config bytes and expected BUILD_ID/serving artifact identities against the existing verified handoff;reject mismatch without replacing the prior handoff,and bind served HTML to that expected build. Keep any permitted disposable cache exceptions explicit.

findings.issue: The post-termination port probe computes available and saves portReleased,but never asserts it. A false result does not throw or invalidate verified;the later if(verified) path can still publish verification.json/reusable-build.json and return success.
findings.impact: A failed required cleanup observation can be represented by a successful QA command,leaving autonomous callers with green status despite an unreleased port or retained listener. Do not signal an unrelated replacement listener;the correct action is a truthful failure. The saved successful run records portReleased:true,so no actual current leak is inferred.
findings.reproduction: Read-only Node24 control executed the exact extracted port-check/save snippet with an in-memory net stub returning an occupied-port result and in-memory save. It returned normally and recorded portReleased:false. Subsequent publication is guarded only by verified,not cleanup success. No real socket,server,signal or filesystem write was used in this control.
findings.fix_direction: Require successful owned-child shutdown and port-release verification before publishing successful verification/handoff;on failure return nonzero and retain a failure record without declaring cleanup complete.
